subject: eocrinoidea
text:
Theca of adjacent or imbricate plates, with or without transsutural
epispires; subvective appendages generally erect, often biserial
brachioles (arranged in two to five groups) confined to adoral end of
theca, arising from generally distinct oral surface (tegmen) bearing
central mouth; theca globular or flattened, often composed of numerous,
irregularly arranged plates; attachment appendage either an irregularly
plated holdfast or a true stem. (Modified from Sprinkle 1973, p. 58;
Ubaghs 1978b, p. T362; Broadhead 1980, p. 125; for an alternative
view, see Broadhead 1982.)

subject: ampheristocystidae
text:
Eocrinoids with definite regular tegmen consisting of orals and fixed
ambulacrals; theca fusiform; the- cal plates moderate in number,
fairly regularly arranged in a few, mostly closed circlets; five
ambulacra terminating as single facets on oral–oral sutures, bearing
biserial trunk with brachioles. Stem, when present, crinoid-like.

subject: ampheristocystis
text:
Theca fusiform; tegmen composed of six large orals and five large
suborals, plus a central and a few smaller ambulacrals; periproct
terminal on tube-like projection; hydropore on suboral–oral suture
in CD interray; no visible gonopore; well developed stem on some
specimens.

subject: concentricus_frest_2005
text:
Aboral thecal plates ornamented by raised concentric ridges;
tegminals nodose; small, elongate fusi- form theca constricted
slightly below tegmen; five or six thecal plate circlets,
adorally interrupted and aborally complete; large stem facet
(or base), about one-third maximum thecal diameter.
